mainTopic: Unspecified vows are treated strictly but explanations leniently, and רבי זירא's answer to the contradiction from doubtful נזירות
overview: This amud opens a new משנה with a rule for vows whose wording could mean two things. If the person gave no explanation, the vow is treated strictly, but if he explains that he meant the lenient meaning, we accept him. The משנה gives examples: salted meat and libation wine (שלמים or עבודה זרה), חרם (to Heaven or to כהנים), מעשר (animal or grain tithe), and תרומה (the Temple chamber fund or the granary gift). A vow works only when it compares an item to something holy through a vow, like a קרבן, and not to something the Torah forbids on its own or that is not forbidden at all. רבי מאיר reads every unexplained vow strictly. רבי יהודה says it depends on what the word means to people where the vow was made, so the rule differs between יהודה and the גליל. The גמרא then asks how unclear vows can be strict when another משנה says a doubt about נזירות is lenient. רבי זירא answers that the two משניות follow different תנאים, proving it from a ברייתא where the רבנן and רבי אליעזר argue about consecrating a כוי. The גמרא begins showing that whoever puts his money into doubt also puts himself into doubt, and this idea continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The general rule: unclear vows are strict, explanations are lenient
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with its principle: סתם נדרים להחמיר, ופירושם להקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: Vows said without details are treated strictly, but when the person explains what he meant, we go with the lenient explanation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a general rule about vows whose wording could mean two things. It is setting up the examples that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone makes a vow that could be read as binding or as not binding, and he gives no explanation, we assume it is binding. But if he says he meant the meaning that makes the vow fail, we believe him. The next steps show exactly how this works.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Vows said without details, so their meaning is unclear
To be strict
Their explanation, when the person says what he meant
To be lenient

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Unspecified vows are treated stringently,
but their specification is treated leniently.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ambiguous vow with no explanation is binding, but the vower's lenient explanation is accepted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle drives the rest of the משנה and the גמרא's discussion that follows.

steps.title: First example: like salted meat or like libation wine
steps.stepSummary: A vow comparing an item to salted meat or יין נסך could refer to שלמים (binding) or to עבודה זרה (not binding). Without explanation, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If someone said, 'This is upon me like salted meat,' or 'like libation wine': if he meant the meat or wine of a שלמים offering, the item is forbidden. If he meant the meat or wine of עבודה זרה, the item is permitted. If he did not say, the item is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first example of the general rule. It uses salted meat and libation wine, which could belong either to a קרבן or to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing an item to a קרבן works, because a קרבן becomes forbidden through a person's vow. Comparing it to עבודה זרה does not work, because the Torah forbids עבודה זרה on its own, not through a vow. When he gives no explanation, we take the strict reading.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? The משנה is introducing examples
This is upon me, a standard vow formula
Salted meat
Libation wine, poured as an offering
Peace-offerings, a type of קרבן
Idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: In this משנה, 'אסור' means the vow takes effect and the item becomes forbidden to him. 'מותר' means the vow did not work at all.

phrases.english: How so? If one said: This is upon me like salted meat,
phrases.notes: Offerings were salted before going on the altar, so 'salted meat' can point to a קרבן.

phrases.english: or: like libation wine,
if he vowed in reference to that of a peace-offering, it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אִם בְּשֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נָדַר — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: If he vowed in reference to that of idol worship, it is permitted.
And if he said it without specification, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First illustration of the general rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salted meat or libation wine: if he meant שלמים, the item is forbidden. If he meant עבודה זרה, it is permitted. If he gave no explanation, it is forbidden.

steps.title: Second example: like a חרם
steps.stepSummary: A vow comparing an item to a חרם could mean a חרם to Heaven (binding) or a חרם to כהנים (not binding). Without explanation, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'This is upon me like a חרם': if he meant a חרם to Heaven, the item is forbidden. If he meant a חרם given to the כהנים, the item is permitted. If he did not say, the item is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second example of the same rule, this time using the word חרם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרם to Heaven is holy, dedicated to the בית המקדש, so comparing an item to it makes the vow work. A חרם to כהנים is just a gift that goes to the כהן, and it is not forbidden at all, so comparing an item to it does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: An item dedicated by a pledge
A חרם dedicated to Heaven, which is holy
A חרם given as a gift to the כהנים
Forbidden (the vow works) / permitted (the vow fails)

phrases.english: If one said: This is upon me like a dedication,
if he meant like a dedication to Heaven, it is forbidden,
and if he meant like a dedication to priests, it is permitted.
And if he said it without specification, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second illustration of the same rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חרם: if he meant a חרם to Heaven, the item is forbidden. If he meant a חרם to כהנים, it is permitted. If he gave no explanation, it is forbidden.

steps.title: Third example: like מעשר
steps.stepSummary: A vow comparing an item to מעשר could mean מעשר בהמה (binding) or grain tithe from the threshing floor (not binding). Without explanation, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'This is upon me like מעשר': if he meant animal tithe, the item is forbidden. If he meant the tithe from the threshing floor, the item is permitted. If he did not say, the item is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its third example of the rule, using the word מעשר. One more example, תרומה, follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה is holy, like a קרבן, so comparing an item to it makes the vow work. The grain tithe given to the לויים has no holiness, so comparing an item to it does not create a vow. Here too, if he gave no explanation, we read the vow strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithe
Animal tithe, which is holy
Grain tithe from the threshing floor, given to the לויים
He vowed

steps.whatToRemember: In every case so far the pattern is the same. If he meant the holy option (שלמים, a חרם to Heaven, מעשר בהמה), the item is forbidden. If he meant the other option, it is permitted. If he gave no explanation, it is forbidden. The תרומה case in the next step follows the same pattern.

phrases.english: If one said: This is upon me like tithes,
if he vowed meaning like the animal tithe, it is forbidden.
And if he meant that of the threshing floor, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: The 'threshing floor' tithe is grain given to the לויים, the tithe taken from the harvest.

phrases.english: And if he said it without specification, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third illustration of the rule; the תרומה case follows in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר: if he meant מעשר בהמה, the item is forbidden. If he meant the grain tithe, it is permitted. If he gave no explanation, it is forbidden.

steps.title: A vow 'like תרומה': רבי מאיר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: A vow comparing an item to תרומה is binding if he meant תרומת הלשכה, not binding if he meant תרומת הגורן, and forbidden if he did not say which, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'This is to me like תרומה': if he meant the Temple chamber collection, it is forbidden. If he meant the granary תרומה, it is permitted. If he did not specify, it is forbidden. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one more example of a vow word with two possible meanings. As before, an unexplained vow is treated strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומת הלשכה is money set aside for the קרבנות, so it is a vowed, sacred item, and comparing to it makes a real vow. תרומת הגורן is a Torah gift to the כהן, not something created by a vow, so comparing to it does nothing. רבי מאיר keeps the משנה's rule: without an explanation, we assume the stricter meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple chamber fund (from the half-shekel) used to buy communal קרבנות
The portion of grain given to the כהן at the threshing floor
Unspecified; said without explaining what he meant
He vowed; here, he had in mind when making the vow

phrases.english: If one says: 'This is hereby forbidden to me like תרומה,'
if he vowed meaning like the Temple chamber collection, it is forbidden.
And if he meant the תרומה of the granary, it is permitted.
And if he said it without specifying, it is forbidden.
These are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of ambiguous vow terms (after the cases of salted meat, חרם, and מעשר), now with תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified vow 'like תרומה' is forbidden, since it may refer to תרומת הלשכה (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: רבי יהודה: It depends on local usage
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that unspecified תרומה and חרמים are judged by what each region normally means by the word.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: An unspecified תרומה vow is forbidden in יהודה but permitted in the גליל, because the people of the גליל don't know about the Temple chamber collection. Unspecified חרמים are permitted in יהודה but forbidden in the גליל, because the people of the גליל don't know about חרמי כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר. He says we don't automatically choose the strict meaning; we go by what the word means to people where the vow was made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the גליל, far from the בית המקדש, 'תרומה' means only the granary gift, so the vow is not binding there. But in the גליל 'חרם' means only a חרם to Heaven, so a חרם vow is binding there. In יהודה it is the other way around: 'תרומה' can mean the chamber fund, so it is forbidden, while 'חרם' is taken as a חרם to כהנים, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Judea, the region near the בית המקדש
The Galilee, the northern region farther from the בית המקדש
They are familiar with; they know about
Items dedicated as a חרם that go to the כהנים (not binding as a vow)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the גליל is always the lenient place. For תרומה the גליל is lenient, but for חרמים the גליל is strict. Each time, ask which meaning the local people actually know.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a big idea in נדרים: a vow can be read by how people normally speak (לשון בני אדם), and not only by the strictest possible meaning.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: סְתַם תְּרוּמָה, בִּיהוּדָה — אֲסוּרָה,
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: Unspecified תרומה in יהודה is forbidden,
in the גליל it is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין אַנְשֵׁי גָלִיל מַכִּירִין אֶת תְּרוּמַת הַלִּשְׁכָּה.
phrases.english: because the people of the גליל are not familiar with the Temple chamber collection.
Unspecified dedications (חרמים) in יהודה are permitted,
in the גליל they are forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין אַנְשֵׁי גָלִיל מַכִּירִין אֶת חֶרְמֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים.
phrases.english: because the people of the גליל are not familiar with dedications to the כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: סְתַם תְּרוּמָה, בִּיהוּדָה אֲסוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי מאיר's automatic stringency and adds the idea of regional usage, applying it both to תרומה and to the חרם case from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unspecified vows are judged by local usage: תרומה is forbidden in יהודה and permitted in the גליל; חרמים are permitted in יהודה and forbidden in the גליל.

steps.title: But unclear נזירות is treated leniently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that unclear vows are strict, using a משנה that says a doubt about נזירות is lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But didn't we learn in a משנה: A doubt about נזירות is treated leniently?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by attacking the משנה's first rule, סתם נדרים להחמיר. It points to another משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נזירות is a kind of vow. If unclear vows are strict, then an unclear נזירות should also be strict. Yet that other משנה says it is lenient, so the two משניות seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a contradiction from a משנה)
A doubt whether someone became a נזיר
To be lenient

phrases.english: גמרא: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
A doubt about נזירות is treated leniently?
phrases.notes: This is from טהרות 4:12. Since נזירות is a type of vow, it seems to clash with 'unclear vows are strict.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא, challenging the משנה's opening principle from step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נזירות is a vow, and another משנה rules that a doubt about it is lenient. That contradicts treating unclear vows strictly.

steps.title: רבי זירא: The two משניות follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the lenient נזירות משנה follows רבי אליעזר, while our משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It's not difficult. That משנה follows רבי אליעזר, and this משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא settles the contradiction by saying the two משניות simply reflect two opinions in a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to make the two משניות agree. The 'doubt is lenient' משנה matches רבי אליעזר, and our 'unclear vows are strict' משנה matches the רבנן who argue with him. The next step brings the source for this מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; introduces an answer
This one ... that one; assigns each source to a different view
The Sages, the majority view

phrases.english: רבי זירא said: It is not difficult:
This one is רבי אליעזר, and this one is the רבנן.
phrases.notes: The lenient נזירות משנה follows רבי אליעזר. Our strict משנה follows the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each source to a different תנא (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to express one shared view on doubtful vows, so they clashed.
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect a מחלוקת: רבנן treat a doubtful vow strictly, and רבי אליעזר treats it leniently.

steps.title: The ברייתא of consecrating a כוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא proves the מחלוקת from a ברייתא about whether a כוי is included when someone consecrates his wild and domestic animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One who consecrates his wild animals and his domestic animals has consecrated the כוי too. רבי אליעזר says: He has not consecrated the כוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a ברייתא to show that רבי אליעזר and the רבנן really do argue about how a doubtful case fits into a person's words of dedication.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כוי is an animal whose category is uncertain: maybe wild, maybe domestic. The רבנן say his dedication covers it anyway, so a doubtful case is treated strictly, like our משנה. רבי אליעזר says it is not covered, so a doubtful case is treated leniently, like the נזירות משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא; introduces a supporting source
One who consecrates (dedicates to the בית המקדש)
A wild (undomesticated) animal
A domestic animal
An animal whose status is doubtful, maybe wild, maybe domestic

steps.whatToRemember: סתם נדרים להחמיר follows the רבנן, who include doubtful cases (like the כוי) in a person's words. ספק נזירות להקל follows רבי אליעזר, who leaves doubtful cases out.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One who consecrates his wild animals and his domestic animals,
has consecrated the כוי as well.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא הִקְדִּישׁ אֶת הַכּוֹי.
phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says: He has not consecrated the כוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי זירא's claim in step 8 that רבי אליעזר and the רבנן disagree.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר and the רבנן disagree about whether a doubtful case is included in a person's dedication.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about consecrating one's wild and domestic animals, where the רבנן include the כוי and רבי אליעזר does not.

steps.title: How the כוי case connects to doubtful נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the כוי argument carries over to נזירות. Whoever holds that a person puts his money into doubt also holds that he puts himself into doubt. Whoever holds that he does not put his money into doubt holds the same about himself. The second half continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says a person puts his money into doubt holds that he puts himself into doubt too. And the one who says a person does not put his money into doubt holds that himself (also) [does not put himself into doubt — the sentence finishes next].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבי זירא's proof. It shows how the argument about consecrating a כוי (money) matches the argument about a doubtful נזירות (the person himself).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Consecrating animals is about property, while נזירות is about the person's own body, so the גמרא has to bridge the two. It says each side treats both the same way. The רבנן, who include the כוי, would also make a doubtful נזיר vow binding, which fits our strict משנה. רבי אליעזר, who leaves the כוי out, would also be lenient on a doubtful נזיר, which fits the lenient משנה about נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says, meaning the opinion that holds...
His money or property (here, his animals)
Brings in, puts into
Into a doubt, into an unclear situation
His own body, himself (here, taking on נזירות)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the sides. Putting money into doubt is the רבנן, who include the כוי and are strict about a doubtful נזיר. Not putting money into doubt is רבי אליעזר, who leaves out the כוי and is lenient.
steps.whyThisMatters: This bridge is what lets רבי זירא answer the קשיא from step 7. The two משניות no longer contradict each other, because each one follows a different תנא.

phrases.english: The one who said that a person puts his property into doubt
phrases.notes: This is the רבנן, who said that when someone consecrates his wild and domestic animals, the כוי is included.

phrases.english: holds that he puts himself into doubt as well

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מָמוֹנוֹ לָא מְעַיֵּיל לִסְפֵיקָא
phrases.english: And the one who said that a person does not put his property into doubt
holds that himself (also)
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. The sentence ends here: he doesn't put himself into doubt either.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מָמוֹנוֹ מְעַיֵּיל לִסְפֵיקָא גּוּפֵיהּ נָמֵי מְעַיֵּיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It finishes the proof from step 9 by carrying the money-based argument about the כוי over to the person-based case of נזירות.
steps.raayaObject: That our strict משנה follows the רבנן and the lenient נזירות משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The כוי ברייתא, read as a principle about whether a person puts his money into doubt, which is then applied to his own body.
